disposition_vocabulary_note: Grew from three values to five during the disposition pass. 'superseded' was doing two jobs: for a recommendation it meant taken, for a finding it meant the criticised text is gone. Those are separated into 'adopted' and 'corrected'. 'refuted' was added because six claims asserted something the record shows false, which v8 contradicts rather than responds to; without it those claims had no correct disposition.

findings_v8_did_not_address.finding: 'Visibility ... is the whole of what this constraint achieves' asserts an achieved result the mechanism does not demonstrate. v8 narrowed the scope to 'of the declared' and retained the assertion of achievement, which was never the object of the finding.

'Must be legible as wide' is not established by any mechanism: no scope language, interpretation rule, validation, rendering requirement or summary-generation rule enforces it. v8 retained the requirement and added no mechanism.
findings_v8_did_not_address.note: Same defect class as the pair above. v8 corrected this overclaim in the standing-authority constraint and reproduced it in the scope-breadth constraint two paragraphs later.

findings_v8_did_not_address.finding: No chain-link, completeness, traversal or attribution rule is specified. v8 fixed the sentence by withdrawing the claim rather than adding the rule; the absence persists.

The external-evidence specification omits which outputs are affected — visibility, invocation, admission — so v8 says what evidence a scope declaration should carry and not what changes if it is absent.

rule: Edges carry (block_id, content_sha256). An amendment that changes a block's text changes its hash and breaks every edge citing it. Re-linking triggers on hash mismatch, not id absence. Breakage forces per-claim re-adjudication rather than silent carry-forward onto text that no longer says what the claim responded to.
